subject: Coffee & Tea
title: Instant Coffee: Accident or Invention?
description: One-minute skill: Instant Coffee: Accident or Invention?.

hook.text: Instant coffee was first mass-produced in 1910 by George Washington—not the president, but a Belgian-American inventor.

buildup.text: Washington noticed dried coffee residue on his carafe lid. He realized brewed coffee could be dehydrated and reconstituted.

discovery.text: His Red E Coffee launched in 1910. During WWI, soldiers loved it—they called any instant coffee 'a cup of George.'

twist.text: Nestlé's Nescafé (1938) perfected the formula. Brazil's coffee surplus funded the research—too many beans to sell.

climax.text: Today, instant coffee outsells brewed in most of the world. Only in the US and parts of Europe does fresh brewing dominate.

punchline.text: Dried residue on a lid, a wartime staple, a global default. Accidents scale.

quiz.question: What inspired George Washington to create instant coffee?
options: He noticed dried coffee residue on his silver carafe lid could be reconstituted

details.summary: Instant coffee was developed independently by several inventors in the early 1900s, but Nestle's 1938 launch of Nescafe made it a global product. Designed to use up Brazil's surplus coffee stocks, instant coffee became essential military rations during World War II and a household staple afterward.
details.whyItMatters: Instant coffee democratized caffeine access worldwide, making coffee available to billions of people regardless of equipment or brewing skill.
takeaways: Nestle launched Nescafe in 1938 to consume Brazil's surplus beans
World War II soldiers spread the instant coffee habit globally
Instant coffee remains the dominant form in many countries today

faq.question: How is instant coffee actually manufactured from regular coffee beans?
faq.answer: Brewed coffee is concentrated and then dried using either spray drying, which blasts liquid into hot air creating fine powder, or freeze drying, which freezes the liquid and removes water by sublimation, preserving more flavor.

faq.question: Why is instant coffee still more popular than brewed coffee in many countries?
faq.answer: Instant coffee requires no equipment, no filters, and minimal preparation time. In markets where specialty equipment is expensive or unavailable, instant coffee provides affordable, reliable caffeine access for millions.
